entries.definition: A Betaflight recording made from several frame types and a header describing how those fields were encoded and configured.
A high-rate Blackbox sample carrying the flight signals used by most plots and analyses. Airframe decodes both intra and predicted main-frame forms.
The angular-rate command presented to the PID controller. Comparing it with gyro response shows what was requested versus what the craft measured.
The flight controller's measured angular rate. In Airframe, gyroADC is the filtered gyro signal used for ordinary response analysis.
The derivative contribution of the PID controller. It is especially sensitive to high-frequency noise, so its spectrum deserves its own inspection.

The controller contribution based on current processed rate error. It contributes tracking authority, but its recorded output is evidence to compare with the whole response rather than a diagnosis of one gain.
The controller contribution built from accumulated processed error. Its behaviour can also reflect I-term Relax, anti-windup, saturation, and firmware details, so it is not a standalone gain verdict.

A setpoint-based contribution that anticipates commanded motion. It is distinct from feedback terms driven by tracking error, and its recorded output must be interpreted with setpoint, gyro, and saturation evidence.
Electrical motor speed reported through bidirectional DShot. Converting it to mechanical frequency requires the correct motor pole count.
Half the effective sample rate: the highest frequency a sampled signal can represent without aliasing. Airframe reports the observed logging-rate context in Overview.
A missing interval between valid main frames. Gaps can hide or distort the very event under investigation.
A view of signal energy by frequency. Airframe's current result is periodogram-like and displayed in decibels; it is not a universal pass/fail meter.
The time shift introduced between an upstream and downstream signal. Attenuation is useful; delay is the bill, and both belong in the discussion.
A per-motor harmonic filter driven by measured eRPM. Judging its alignment requires valid eRPM data and the correct motor pole count.
A filter that tracks remaining spectral peaks. Following a peak does not identify its mechanical cause, so source evidence and physical inspection remain separate questions.
Airframe's normalized estimate of how gyro output follows setpoint input over time, averaged from qualifying two-second windows using Wiener deconvolution.
A Betaflight excitation that sweeps frequency on an axis. A CHIRP mode flag alone does not guarantee that all channels needed for modern frequency-response analysis were logged.
A frequency-by-frequency measure of how consistently input and output relate in the CHIRP estimate. Airframe uses it to bound reliable response evidence.

Airframe's bounded assessment of one supported CHIRP response across stability margin, robustness, damping, and tracking fidelity. It describes the recorded response and does not prescribe PID values.
Airframe's description of the completeness and quality of the evidence supporting a CHIRP assessment. Confidence is reported separately and does not change Tune Score.
A change in Betaflight's logged 32-bit mode mask. When an event carries no timestamp, Airframe places it using the latest valid main-frame time as context.

Airframe's regular-file workspace, which can keep multiple logs with associated configuration evidence, aircraft settings, names, notes, and view state. Included logs can be exported again as .bbl or .bfl files.
